Lemma
[Existence of curvature bumps] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0278, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0279 ↗ thm:chow-ii-interior-first-derivative-estimate 1. ch14:14.21\group Curvature Positivity

Suppose $|\operatorname {Rm}|\le K$ on $B_{g(0)}(p,r) imes [0,T]$ and the least curvature-operator eigenvalue satisfies $\lambda _1(\operatorname {Rm})(p, au )\ge cK$.

  1. There is $\eta =\eta (n,K,r, au ,c)>0$ such that $\lambda _1(\operatorname {Rm})(x, au )\ge cK/2$ on $B_{g(0)}(p,\eta )$.

  2. If $r\ge cK^{-1/2}$ and $ au \ge cK^{-1}$, there is $\gamma (n,c)>0$ such that the same conclusion holds on $B_{g(0)}(p,\gamma K^{-1/2})$.

Proof

\sketch The local derivative estimate bounds $| abla \operatorname {Rm}(\cdot , au )|$ on the half ball. Along a minimizing $g( au )$-geodesic $ eta $ from $p$ to $x$,

\[ \lambda _1(\operatorname {Rm})(x, au ) \ge cK-\int _ eta | abla \operatorname {Rm}(\cdot , au )|\, ds_{g( au )}. \]

Metric comparison and a sufficiently small $g(0)$-radius make the integral at most $cK/2$, proving the first assertion. Under the hypotheses of the second assertion, Theorem 3 gives $| abla \operatorname {Rm}|\le C(n,c)K^{3/2}$. Taking $\gamma \le \min \{ c/(2C(n,c)),c/2\} $ proves the uniform-radius claim.

□
